entities.name: Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Hatib Bin Abi Balta'ah was a prominent Companion of the Prophet Muhammad, playing a key role in the early Islamic community. Born in Mecca around 580 CE, he was a veteran of the Battle of Badr and participated in numerous other battles alongside Muhammad. Hatib's significance extends beyond his military prowess, as he was a respected leader and mediator within the Muslim community. He is also notable for his involvement in the Council of Medina, where he played a crucial role in the city's governance. Hatib's legacy continues to be felt in the Islamic world, with his name appearing in various hadith collections and his teachings influencing the development of Islamic jurisprudence. He died in Medina during the reign of the Prophet's son-in-law, Abu Bakr. Despite limited information on his personal life, Hatib Bin Abi Balta'ah's contributions to the early Islamic community have earned him a place as one of the most important Companions of the Prophet.
